q: Notices and communications required to be given to a contractor under a works contract are ordinarily treated as duly served when they are:

options.A: Delivered at, or sent by registered post to, the address of the contractor recorded for the purpose in the contract
options.B: Communicated orally to any workman found at the site of the work
options.C: Displayed on the notice board of the divisional office
options.D: Published in a newspaper circulating in the area of the work

e: Under the GCC, notices are duly served when delivered at, or sent by registered post to, the contractor address recorded in the contract, as that is the agreed mode of service.

q: A contractor deputes an authorised representative to remain at the site of a work and to receive instructions on his behalf. Instructions given by the Engineer to that representative at the site are:

options.A: Of no effect until they are separately accepted in writing by the contractor himself
options.B: Binding only if they relate to the supply of materials
options.C: Treated as instructions given to the contractor himself, the representative being authorised to receive them
options.D: Valid only during the working hours of the divisional office

e: Instructions given by the Engineer to the contractor authorised site representative are deemed given to the contractor himself, since the representative is authorised to receive them under the GCC.

q: The insurance policies which a works contractor is required to take for a work under the conditions of contract are to be:

options.A: Taken only after the completion certificate for the work is issued
options.B: Kept in force for the period required by the contract, the contractor producing evidence of the policies and of the payment of premia when called upon
options.C: Assigned to the contractor's banker as security for his borrowings
options.D: Taken in the name of the contractor's labour union

e: The GCC requires the contractor to keep the prescribed insurance policies in force for the contract period and to produce the policies and proof of premium payment when called upon.

q: A works contractor engaging contract labour on a railway work is required, under the labour enactments applicable to him, to maintain and produce for inspection:

options.A: Only the measurement books of the work
options.B: The tender documents of all the works executed by him in the past
options.C: The muster rolls of the railway's own departmental staff
options.D: The prescribed registers and records relating to the labour engaged by him, including their attendance and the wages paid to them

e: Under the Contract Labour Act and allied labour laws, the contractor must maintain and produce prescribed registers and records of labour engaged, their attendance and wages paid.

q: A works contract containing an arbitration clause is terminated by the Railways on account of the contractor's defaults, and a dispute thereafter arises in connection with that contract. The arbitration clause in such a case:

options.A: Comes to an end along with the contract, so that the dispute can be pursued only in a civil court
options.B: Survives the termination of the contract for the purpose of the settlement of disputes arising out of or in connection with the contract
options.C: Is replaced by the decision of the tender committee which awarded the work
options.D: Can be invoked only by the Railways and not by the contractor

e: Under Sec 16 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the arbitration clause is separable from the main contract and survives its termination for disputes arising from the contract.

q: During the pendency of arbitral proceedings in a works dispute, the parties reach a settlement of the dispute between themselves and request the arbitral tribunal to record it. The tribunal thereupon:

options.A: Records the settlement in the form of an arbitral award on the agreed terms, which has the same status and effect as any other arbitral award
options.B: Returns the case to the tender committee for a fresh recommendation
options.C: Refuses to take notice of the settlement, the proceedings having already commenced
options.D: Records the settlement only as a noting in the case file, with no legal effect

e: Under Sec 30 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, a settlement recorded by the tribunal as an award on agreed terms has the same status and effect as any other arbitral award.

q: In arbitral proceedings arising out of a works contract, the question of the costs of the arbitration, including the fee of the arbitral tribunal, is dealt with by:

options.A: The contractor alone, who invariably bears the entire costs
options.B: The court which issued the decree in the case
options.C: The Accounts office, as part of the final bill of the work
options.D: The arbitral tribunal, which has the discretion to determine whether costs are payable, by whom and in what amount, unless the parties have agreed otherwise

e: Under Sec 31A of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the tribunal has discretion to fix costs, decide by whom and in what amount they are payable, unless the parties agreed otherwise.

q: In the Hybrid Annuity Model of executing a project through public-private partnership, the project cost is met in the manner that:

options.A: The entire cost is recovered by the private partner from the users of the facility as toll
options.B: The private partner meets the entire cost and receives nothing from the authority during the concession period
options.C: The authority bears the entire cost departmentally and the private partner only maintains the facility
options.D: A part of the project cost is paid by the authority during the construction period and the balance is paid to the private partner in annuity instalments during the operation period

e: In Hybrid Annuity Model, part of the project cost is paid by the authority during construction and the balance is paid to the private partner as annuity instalments during operation.

q: A zonal (works) contract entered into by a division for a zone of the division serves principally to:

options.A: Arrange the petty and ordinary works and repairs arising in that zone during the period of the contract, at the rates accepted under it, without inviting tenders for each small work separately
options.B: Execute a single large project situated within that zone
options.C: Procure the stores required by all the depots of the zone
options.D: Engage the establishment required for the regular maintenance of the section

e: A zonal contract covers petty and ordinary works and repairs arising in a zone during its currency at accepted rates, avoiding separate tenders for each small work, as per the Engineering Code.

q: As regards the tools and plant used on a work, the position in the estimates and accounts of works is that:

options.A: All tools and plant, whether special or ordinary, are charged directly to the work at their full purchase price
options.B: Special tools and plant purchased specially for a work are charged directly to that work, while the cost of ordinary tools and plant is recovered through the percentage tools-and-plant charges
options.C: No charge on account of tools and plant is ever made to a work
options.D: Tools and plant are charged to the personal account of the Engineer supervising the work

e: Special tools and plant bought specially for a work are charged direct to that work; ordinary tools and plant cost is recovered through percentage tools and plant charges, per works accounts rules.

q: In the briefing note placed before a Tender Committee for a work, the reasonableness of the rates offered by the lowest tenderer is ordinarily examined with reference to:

options.A: The rates quoted by the highest tenderer for the same work
options.B: The personal assessment of the sectional officer supervising the section
options.C: The estimated rates for the work and the last accepted rates for similar items of work
options.D: The rates prevailing in the tenders of another zonal railway in every case

e: Reasonableness of the lowest rates is judged in the tender briefing note against the estimate rates and last accepted rates for similar work, the standard tender committee test.

q: On the completion and taking over of a work, the asset created by it finds a place in the accounts of the Railways through:

options.A: The contractor's ledger maintained in the Accounts office
options.B: The suspense head 'Demands Recoverable'
options.C: The traffic earnings account of the division
options.D: The Block Account, which records the capital-at-charge represented by the assets created

e: On completion, the asset created is capitalised in the Block Account, which records the capital-at-charge of railway assets, under the Financial and Engineering Codes.

q: Before the construction of a private siding for a firm is taken up, the arrangement between the Railways and the firm is formalised through:

options.A: A siding agreement executed between the Railways and the firm, settling the cost, the land, the maintenance and the other terms on which the siding will be provided and worked
options.B: A licence for the sale of goods from the premises of the firm
options.C: A resolution of the gram panchayat of the area in which the siding is situated
options.D: The issue of a works tender to the firm itself

e: A private siding is provided only under a siding agreement with the firm settling cost, land, maintenance and working terms, as required by the Engineering Code siding rules.

q: A work executed by the Railways as a deposit work for an outside body is distinguished, in the matter of the asset created, from a railway work in that:

options.A: The asset created is entered in the Block Account of the Railways as railway property
options.B: The asset created belongs to the body at whose cost the work was executed, and is not added to the assets of the Railways
options.C: No record of the work is maintained by the Railways at all
options.D: The asset is treated as a stores balance of the depot executing the work

e: In a deposit work the asset belongs to the outside body at whose cost it is executed; it is not added to railway assets or the Block Account, per deposit works rules.

q: Funds for a work are available in the budget allotment of a division, but the cost of the work exceeds the powers of sanction delegated to the authority proposing to sanction it. In such a case:

options.A: The work may be sanctioned by that authority, availability of funds being sufficient by itself
options.B: The work may be split into two works so as to bring each within that authority's powers
options.C: The work cannot be sanctioned by that authority, the availability of funds not conferring on it a power of sanction which it does not possess, and the sanction of the competent higher authority is necessary
options.D: The sanction may be accorded subject to ratification by the Accounts branch at the end of the year

e: Availability of funds does not confer power of sanction. A work beyond delegated powers needs sanction of the competent higher authority, and splitting to evade powers is prohibited.

q: A works contractor, instead of invoking the arbitration clause of his contract, files a suit in a civil court on a matter covered by that clause. The Railways bring the arbitration agreement to the notice of the court at the earliest stage. Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the court is ordinarily required to:

options.A: Decide the suit itself, the arbitration clause notwithstanding
options.B: Refer the parties to arbitration, where a valid arbitration agreement covering the matter exists
options.C: Dismiss the suit with costs in every case
options.D: Direct the parties to settle the matter through the Tender Committee

e: Under Sec 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, where a valid arbitration agreement covers the matter, the court must refer the parties to arbitration on timely application.

q: An arbitrator appointed for a works dispute dies during the proceedings and his mandate accordingly terminates. Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the vacancy so caused is filled by:

options.A: Treating the arbitration agreement as extinguished
options.B: The senior-most officer of the Railway, acting on his own
options.C: Appointing a substitute arbitrator according to the same rules that applied to the appointment of the arbitrator being replaced
options.D: Referring the dispute afresh to a civil court

e: Under Sec 15 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, a substitute arbitrator is appointed according to the same rules that applied to the arbitrator being replaced.

q: Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, an arbitral tribunal dealing with a works dispute is empowered, during the proceedings, to make an interim arbitral award:

options.A: On any matter with respect to which it may make a final arbitral award
options.B: Only on the question of its own jurisdiction
options.C: Only after the final hearing of the dispute is concluded
options.D: Only with the prior permission of the appointing authority

e: Under Sec 31(6) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the tribunal may make an interim award on any matter on which it may make a final award.

q: In a domestic arbitration arising out of a works contract, the arbitral award is required, as a general rule under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, to:

options.A: Be an oral award communicated to the parties
options.B: Contain no reasons, even where the parties have not agreed otherwise
options.C: Be approved by the General Manager before it is delivered
options.D: State the reasons upon which it is based, unless the parties have agreed that no reasons are to be given or the award records an agreed settlement

e: Under Sec 31(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the award must state reasons, unless parties agreed no reasons are needed or it records an agreed settlement.

q: In arbitral proceedings on a works dispute, the respondent contractor, despite due notice, fails to file his statement of defence and does not appear at the hearing. Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the tribunal may:

options.A: Treat the failure as an admission of all the claims of the Railway
options.B: Continue the proceedings and make the award on the evidence before it, without treating the failure by itself as an admission of the allegations
options.C: Terminate the proceedings forthwith in favour of the respondent
options.D: Refer the dispute back to the Engineer for a fresh decision

e: Under Sec 25 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, if the respondent defaults, the tribunal continues and awards on the evidence before it, without treating default as admission.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where the parties to a works contract have agreed upon a particular place as the seat of arbitration, the courts at that seat exercise supervisory jurisdiction over the arbitration.
2. A mere venue or place of hearing of the arbitration, without more, is the same thing as the juridical seat of the arbitration.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: an agreed seat gives its courts supervisory jurisdiction. Statement 2 is wrong: a mere venue of hearing is not the juridical seat, so only 1 is correct.

q: 'Patent illegality' as a ground for setting aside an arbitral award in a works dispute, under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, refers broadly to:

options.A: Any error of fact made by the tribunal in appreciating the evidence
options.B: A disagreement of the court with the interpretation of the contract adopted by the tribunal
options.C: An illegality apparent on the face of the award, such as a decision contrary to the substantive law or to the terms of the contract itself
options.D: A delay by the tribunal in making the award after the close of hearings

e: Patent illegality means an illegality apparent on the face of the award, such as a decision contrary to substantive law or to the contract terms, a Sec 34 ground for setting aside.

q: Where an arbitral tribunal in a works dispute appoints an expert to report to it on specific technical issues, the position under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is that:

options.A: The expert's report is binding on the tribunal in all respects
options.B: The expert thereby becomes a co-arbitrator of the dispute
options.C: The parties cannot question the expert or place their own expert evidence before the tribunal
options.D: The parties may question the expert at a hearing and present their own expert witnesses on the points at issue

e: Under Sec 26 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, parties may question the tribunal expert at a hearing and present their own expert witnesses on the points at issue.

q: As regards the law of limitation, the position of arbitral proceedings arising out of a works contract under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is that:

options.A: No period of limitation applies to claims placed before an arbitral tribunal
options.B: The provisions of the Limitation Act, 1963 apply to arbitrations in the same manner as they apply to proceedings in a court
options.C: Limitation for arbitration claims is governed solely by the General Conditions of Contract
options.D: A time-barred claim must invariably be entertained by the tribunal on merits

e: Under Sec 43 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the Limitation Act, 1963 applies to arbitrations as it applies to proceedings in a court.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a bank guarantee from a letter of credit in contract transactions?

options.A: A bank guarantee is an undertaking of the bank to pay on the default of the principal debtor, whereas a letter of credit is an undertaking to pay the beneficiary against presentation of the stipulated documents
options.B: A bank guarantee is payable only against shipping documents, whereas a letter of credit is payable on mere demand
options.C: Both instruments are issued by the beneficiary of the contract
options.D: Neither instrument involves any undertaking by a bank

e: A bank guarantee is payable on default of the principal debtor, while a letter of credit is payable to the beneficiary against presentation of the stipulated documents.

q: A credit balance appearing under the suspense head 'Miscellaneous Works Advances' in connection with works would ordinarily represent:

options.A: Amounts recoverable from contractors for materials supplied to them
options.B: The value of materials lying unconsumed at the sites of works
options.C: Advances paid to contractors which remain unrecovered at the close of the contract
options.D: Amounts received from outside parties in connection with works, which are held pending their adjustment or the execution of the work concerned

e: A credit under Miscellaneous Works Advances represents amounts received from outside parties for works, held pending adjustment or execution of the work concerned.

q: On a reconciliation of a work, the Material-at-Site account of the work is found to show a credit balance instead of the usual debit balance. Such a credit balance is abnormal and ordinarily indicates that:

options.A: A saving has been achieved in the sanctioned estimate of the work
options.B: The work has been completed ahead of its stipulated date
options.C: Credits for materials returned or adjusted have exceeded the debits for materials issued, or that an erroneous posting has been made, calling for investigation and correction
options.D: The contractor has become entitled to a refund of his security deposit

e: A credit balance in Material-at-Site is abnormal as issues should exceed credits; it shows credits for returns or adjustments exceeding debits, or wrong posting, needing investigation.

q: Rails and sleepers for a track work are supplied to the contractor free of cost by the Railways, the contractor having only to lay them. In working out price variation on the contract, the correct treatment of the value of such free-issue materials is that:

options.A: Price variation is payable on their full value as if the contractor had purchased them
options.B: No price variation is admissible on the value of materials supplied free by the Railways, as the contractor bears no price risk on them
options.C: Price variation on them is payable to the Railways by the contractor
options.D: The materials are to be excluded from measurement altogether

e: Price variation compensates the contractor for price risk he bears; no variation is admissible on free-issue railway materials, as he bears no price risk on them, per the PVC clause.

q: On the orders of the Engineer, a portion of a work already executed and covered up is opened up for inspection and testing, and the work so exposed is found to be defective and not in accordance with the contract. The cost of opening up, testing and making good the work is borne by:

options.A: The contractor
options.B: The Railways, in all cases, whether the work is defective or not
options.C: The officer who recorded the measurements of the work
options.D: The insurance company with which the work is insured

e: Under the GCC, if work opened up on the Engineer order is found defective, the cost of opening up, testing and making good is borne by the contractor.

q: Railway land has been given to a party on licence for use as an open storage yard. Without the permission of the Railways, the licensee constructs a permanent building on the land. The correct position is that:

options.A: The construction is permissible, a licence being equivalent to a lease of the land
options.B: The building becomes the property of the licensee and cannot be disturbed
options.C: The Railways must regularise the construction on payment of a nominal fee
options.D: The construction is a breach of the terms of the licence, and the Railways may terminate the licence and require the licensee to remove the structure and restore the land

e: A licence does not create a lease. Unauthorised permanent construction breaches the licence, so Railways may terminate it and require removal of the structure and restoration of land.

q: A private party, without obtaining any way-leave permission, lays a cable across railway land for its own use and continues to use the crossing. The correct course for the Railways is to:

options.A: Treat the crossing as authorised, since no damage has been caused to the track
options.B: Acquire the cable as railway property without any proceedings
options.C: Treat the use as unauthorised occupation of railway land and require the party to remove the cable or obtain permission, recovering the charges and damages leviable for the unauthorised use
options.D: Charge the cost of the cable to the maintenance estimate of the division

e: Laying a cable without way-leave is unauthorised occupation of railway land; Railways must require removal or regular permission and recover leviable charges and damages.

q: The completion of a work is delayed because the contractor's own excavator remained under breakdown for a long period and he made no alternative arrangement. His claim for extension of time on this ground is not tenable because:

options.A: A hindrance caused by the failure of the contractor's own plant and arrangements is attributable to the contractor himself and does not justify extension of time
options.B: Extension of time can be granted only by the Railway Board
options.C: Breakdown of plant is treated as a force majeure event in all cases
options.D: The contractor was required to insure the plant with the Railways themselves

e: Extension of time is for hindrances not attributable to the contractor. Breakdown of his own plant with no alternative arrangement is his own default, so no extension is justified.

q: A work stands completed and taken over, but the contractor, even after due notice, leaves his plant, sheds and surplus materials on railway land at the site beyond the period allowed for clearing it. The Railways may:

options.A: Appropriate the plant and materials as their own property without any accounting
options.B: Pay the contractor rent for the use of his plant for the period of occupation
options.C: Extend the defect liability period of the work indefinitely on this account alone
options.D: Remove the plant and materials from the site and recover the cost of removal and of restoring the site from the amounts due to the contractor or from his security deposit

e: Under the GCC, on failure to clear the site after notice, Railways may remove the contractor plant and materials and recover removal and restoration cost from dues or security deposit.

q: In the Finance vetting of a detailed estimate of a work, a large provision has been made as a single lump sum for a group of items, without any supporting details or calculations. The objection properly taken to such a provision is that:

options.A: Lump-sum provisions are permissible only in deposit works
options.B: A detailed estimate must be supported by item-wise details and calculations, and a substantial lump-sum provision without such support cannot be accepted as in order
options.C: The provision should have been made under contingencies of the estimate
options.D: The provision can be accepted if the executive certifies that it will not be exceeded

e: A detailed estimate must be supported by item-wise details and calculations for Finance vetting; a large unsupported lump sum cannot be accepted as in order.

q: The rates adopted in the detailed estimate of a work of a zonal railway have been taken bodily from the schedule of rates of another railway, without any analysis with reference to local conditions. This course is objectionable principally because:

options.A: Schedules of rates are secret documents of the railway which issues them
options.B: Rates for a work should be based on the schedule of rates of the railway concerned or on an analysis reflecting the local cost of materials, labour and carriage
options.C: Only the Railway Board can adopt rates in an estimate
options.D: Rates adopted from another railway attract departmental charges at a higher rate

e: Estimate rates must be based on the railway own schedule of rates or an analysis reflecting local material, labour and carriage costs, not copied bodily from another railway.

q: A seller accepts an order placed on the Government e-Marketplace at a stated price and thereafter demands a higher price before supplying, citing a rise in the market. The correct position is that:

options.A: The seller is bound by the price of the accepted order and cannot unilaterally revise it, the concluded contract being governed by the terms of the order
options.B: The buyer is bound to pay the higher price demanded by the seller
options.C: The order automatically stands cancelled without any consequence for the seller
options.D: The price is to be refixed by the consignee after delivery of the goods

e: On GeM, the accepted order is a concluded contract at the stated price; the seller is bound by it and cannot unilaterally demand a higher price for market rise.

q: Departmental materials were issued to a contractor for incorporation in a work. On completion of the work, a quantity of such materials remains unused and surplus with the contractor. The correct treatment of the surplus materials is that the contractor must:

options.A: Retain them as his own property against future works of the Railways
options.B: Sell them in the market and retain the sale proceeds
options.C: Hand them over to the incoming contractor of the next work in the section
options.D: Return them to the Railways or pay for their value at the prescribed rate, together with the charges leviable, as the Railways may direct

e: Surplus departmental materials remain railway property; the contractor must return them or pay their value at the prescribed rate with leviable charges, as Railways direct.

q: Midway through a financial year, the allotment for a division's works is curtailed in a budgetary review. The correct course for the executive in regard to its sanctioned works is to:

options.A: Continue incurring liabilities on all works as before, the sanctions being already accorded
options.B: Restrict the progress of expenditure and the incurring of fresh liabilities to the funds actually allotted, surrendering or slowing down works as the reduced allotment requires
options.C: Book the excess expenditure to the works of the following year
options.D: Meet the excess by diverting the deposits received for deposit works

e: Expenditure and fresh liabilities must be kept within the funds actually allotted after a budget cut; works must be surrendered or slowed, not booked elsewhere or from deposits.

q: A work is to be executed by the Railways as an agency work for another Government department. Before the work is actually taken in hand, the essential requirement is that:

options.A: The department concerned accepts the estimate for the work and places the necessary funds at the disposal of the Railways for incurring the expenditure
options.B: The Railways first complete the work and then recover its cost from the department
options.C: The work is included in the Pink Book of the Railways as a railway work
options.D: The contractor for the work is selected by the indenting department itself

e: For an agency work, the other department must first accept the estimate and place funds at the disposal of Railways before the work is taken in hand.

q: The report of a reconnaissance survey of a proposed new railway line ordinarily serves the investment process by:

options.A: Fixing the final alignment of the line on the ground with permanent marks
options.B: Preparing the detailed estimate of the line for technical sanction
options.C: Comparing the alternative alignments examined, with their rough costs and the traffic expected on each, and recommending the alignment that merits detailed investigation
options.D: Acquiring the land required for the selected alignment

e: A reconnaissance survey report compares alternative alignments with rough costs and expected traffic and recommends the alignment meriting detailed investigation.

q: Waterproofing treatment provided over the terrace of a railway building in a works contract serves principally to:

options.A: Increase the load-bearing capacity of the roof slab
options.B: Provide thermal insulation to the rooms below the terrace
options.C: Improve the appearance of the roof surface
options.D: Prevent the seepage and leakage of rainwater through the roof into the rooms below

e: Waterproofing over a terrace is provided to prevent seepage and leakage of rainwater through the roof into the rooms below, which is its functional purpose.

q: A 'sand hump' provided at the end of a catch siding or slip siding on a steep gradient serves to:

options.A: Store sand required for the sanding gear of locomotives
options.B: Arrest and bring to rest a runaway vehicle entering the siding, the wheels sinking into the sand
options.C: Mark the end of the siding for the guidance of drivers
options.D: Drain water away from the end of the siding

e: A sand hump at the end of a catch or slip siding arrests a runaway vehicle by its wheels sinking into the sand, bringing it to rest safely.

q: A 'curtain wall' provided in a framed building constructed under a works contract is:

options.A: A non-load-bearing external wall which encloses the building and carries only its own weight, the loads of the building being carried by the frame
options.B: A load-bearing wall which supports the roof of the building
options.C: A temporary wall erected by the contractor for the protection of the work
options.D: A wall built across a stream to divert its flow during construction

e: A curtain wall is a non-load-bearing external wall enclosing a framed building and carrying only its own weight; the frame carries the building loads.

q: A 'ventilator' provided in the wall of a room of a building is:

options.A: A duct through which the exhaust gases of a diesel generator are discharged
options.B: A glazed panel provided in the roof for admitting daylight
options.C: A small opening, usually provided high up in the wall above a door or window, for the ventilation of the room
options.D: A recess in the wall for fixing an electrical distribution board

e: A ventilator is a small opening usually high in a wall, above a door or window, provided for ventilation of the room.

q: The 'kerb' provided along the edge of a road or a paved area in a work serves to:

options.A: Carry the storm-water drain of the road beneath the pavement
options.B: Support the girders of an adjoining bridge
options.C: Store the surplus earth excavated from the road formation
options.D: Form a raised edge which separates the carriageway or pavement from the adjoining shoulder or footpath and protects its edge

e: A kerb is the raised edge separating carriageway or pavement from the adjoining shoulder or footpath and protecting the pavement edge.

q: Well before the completion date of a work, the contractor writes to the Railways stating plainly that he will not execute the work further. The Railways may treat this 'anticipatory breach' of the contract as:

options.A: A mere expression of opinion which has no legal consequence
options.B: A breach of the contract entitling the Railways to determine the contract and pursue the remedies available for the contractor's default, without waiting for the completion date
options.C: A ground for granting the contractor an extension of time
options.D: An automatic foreclosure of the contract at the contractor's cost in all respects

e: A clear refusal to perform further is anticipatory breach; under contract law Railways may treat it as breach, determine the contract and pursue default remedies without waiting.

q: A contractor abandons a work and the Railways take up the completion of the balance work. Several months are allowed to pass without any step being taken, during which the rates of labour and materials rise sharply, and the extra cost of completion increases accordingly. In recovering the extra cost from the defaulting contractor, the principle of mitigation of damages means that:

options.A: The defaulting contractor must bear the enhanced cost, however long the Railways may delay
options.B: The Railways can recover nothing from the defaulting contractor in such a case
options.C: The extra cost is to be shared equally between the Railways and the contractor
options.D: The party suffering from a breach is expected to take reasonable steps to minimise its loss, and cannot recover the additional loss which such reasonable steps would have avoided

e: Under the mitigation principle in Sec 73 of the Contract Act, the injured party must take reasonable steps to minimise loss and cannot recover loss such steps would have avoided.

q: For an item of a work, the specification permits the use of a material 'or its approved equivalent'. The contractor proposes to use an equivalent material of another make. The correct course is that:

options.A: The equivalent material may be used only after the approval of the Engineer is obtained, and its use does not by itself entitle the contractor to a higher rate for the item
options.B: The contractor may use any material he chooses without informing the Engineer
options.C: The use of an equivalent material automatically converts the item into an extra item
options.D: Equivalent materials can never be accepted on a railway work

e: An approved equivalent needs the Engineer approval before use, and its use alone does not entitle the contractor to a higher rate for the item, per the GCC.

q: In the running bill of a work, the contractor claims payment for an item of work which, though stated to have been executed, does not find a place in the measurements recorded in the Measurement Book. The claim is not payable because:

options.A: Running bills can cover only items of the original tender schedule
options.B: The contractor has not furnished a separate invoice for the item
options.C: Payment under a works contract is made only for work actually measured and recorded in the Measurement Book, and work not so recorded cannot be certified for payment
options.D: The item can be paid only in the final bill of the work

e: Payment under a works contract is only for work actually measured and recorded in the Measurement Book; unrecorded work cannot be certified or paid in a running bill.

q: A party to a works contract sends a written invitation to the other party to settle their dispute through conciliation, but the other party rejects the invitation. Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the position is that:

options.A: Conciliation proceedings are deemed to have commenced on the date of the invitation
options.B: Conciliation proceedings do not commence, conciliation being a voluntary process which begins only when the other party accepts the invitation in writing
options.C: The dispute stands automatically referred to arbitration
options.D: The inviting party may compel conciliation through the court

e: Under Sec 61 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, conciliation is voluntary and commences only when the other party accepts the invitation in writing; rejection means no commencement.

q: Departmental materials issued to a contractor for use on a work remain, until consumed on the work, the property of the Railways. It follows from this that the contractor is required to:

options.A: Insure the materials in his own name as his own property
options.B: Show the materials as his own stock in his accounts
options.C: Sell any materials damaged in his custody and retain the proceeds
options.D: Keep a proper account of the materials received, consumed and in balance, and produce it for verification, making good any shortage found with him

e: Departmental materials remain railway property until consumed, so the contractor must account for materials received, consumed and in balance, produce it for verification and make good shortages.

q: Measurement Books used for recording the measurements of works are treated as important original records, and accordingly they are:

options.A: Issued with their pages consecutively numbered, kept in safe custody and produced for check and audit as required
options.B: Kept in the personal custody of the contractor executing the work
options.C: Destroyed as soon as the final bill of the work is paid
options.D: Maintained in duplicate by the contractor and the Engineer separately

e: Measurement Books are important original records; they are issued with pages consecutively numbered, kept in safe custody and produced for check and audit as required.

q: After a works contract has been concluded, a State Government increases a statutory levy on a material used in the work and the contractor claims reimbursement of the increase as a matter of course. The correct position is that:

options.A: Every increase in a statutory levy after the award is automatically payable by the Railways
options.B: The contractor can in no case be compensated for any statutory levy
options.C: Such a claim is governed by the provisions of the contract regarding statutory variations in taxes and levies, and is admissible only to the extent and in the manner those provisions allow
options.D: The increase is to be met from the contingencies provision of the estimate

e: Reimbursement of a post-contract rise in a statutory levy is governed by the contract provisions on statutory variations, and is admissible only as and to the extent they allow.

q: At the site of a railway work, the contractor is found employing young children as labourers on construction work. The employment is objectionable and must be stopped because:

options.A: Children may be employed on works only with the permission of the Engineer
options.B: Children below the prescribed age can be employed only on piece-rate items
options.C: The employment of children in such work is prohibited by law, and the contractor, as the employer, is liable for the contravention
options.D: The wages payable to children are not covered by the schedule of rates

e: Employment of children below the prescribed age in construction work is prohibited by law, and the contractor as employer is liable for the contravention, so it must be stopped.

q: The abstracts of the labour enactments and the notices regarding hours of work, rest days and wage payment, which a contractor is required to exhibit for the information of the labour engaged on a work, are to be displayed:

options.A: In the office of the Divisional Railway Manager
options.B: Only in the head office of the contractor's firm
options.C: Inside the Measurement Book of the work
options.D: At a conspicuous place at or near the site of the work, where the labour engaged on it can see them

e: Abstracts of labour enactments and notices on hours, rest and wages must be displayed at a conspicuous place at or near the work site, where the labour can see them.

q: On the making of an arbitral award in a works dispute, signed copies of the award are required, under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, to be:

options.A: Delivered to each party to the arbitration
options.B: Sent only to the party in whose favour the award is made
options.C: Retained by the tribunal until its fees are settled by the Railway Board
options.D: Published in the Gazette of India

e: Under Sec 31(5) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, signed copies of the arbitral award are to be delivered to each party to the arbitration.

q: During arbitral proceedings in a works dispute, the parties themselves arrive at a settlement of the dispute and jointly request the tribunal to record it. Apart from recording the settlement as an award on agreed terms where the tribunal does not object, the tribunal is empowered by the Act to:

options.A: Punish the parties for having settled the dispute between themselves
options.B: Continue the proceedings to a final award on merits in every case
options.C: Encourage the settlement of the dispute by the parties, including through mediation or conciliation during the proceedings, with their agreement
options.D: Transfer the dispute to the Tender Committee for recording the settlement

e: Under Sec 30(1) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the tribunal may encourage settlement by the parties, including through mediation or conciliation, with their agreement.

q: An outside body, for which a deposit work is in progress, directs the Railways in writing to stop the work altogether and not to execute it further. The correct course in such a case is that:

options.A: The Railways must complete the work from their own funds in the public interest
options.B: The work is brought to a close, the expenditure incurred being adjusted against the amount deposited by the body and the balance, if any, being dealt with as per the terms on which the deposit was made
options.C: The contractor executing the work must bear the expenditure already incurred
options.D: The deposit amount stands forfeited to the Railways in full

e: On the depositing body directing stoppage, the deposit work is closed, expenditure incurred is adjusted against its deposit and the balance dealt with as per the deposit terms.

q: A party to a works arbitration wishes to challenge an arbitrator on the ground of circumstances giving rise to justifiable doubts as to his independence or impartiality. Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the challenge is to be made by:

options.A: Filing a suit for the removal of the arbitrator in the first instance
options.B: Sending a written statement of the reasons for the challenge to the arbitral tribunal itself, under the challenge procedure of the Act
options.C: Complaining to the Tender Committee which awarded the work
options.D: Withholding participation in the proceedings without any statement

e: Under Sec 13(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, a challenge to an arbitrator is made by sending a written statement of reasons to the arbitral tribunal itself.

q: A challenge made by a party to an arbitrator in a works dispute is considered by the tribunal and is not accepted. The consequence under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is that:

options.A: The arbitral proceedings stand automatically stayed until a court decides the challenge
options.B: The arbitration agreement ceases to be operative
options.C: The challenging party may get the arbitrator removed by the Engineer at any stage
options.D: The tribunal continues the proceedings and makes its award, and the challenging party may thereafter seek the setting aside of the award on that ground

e: Under Sec 13(4) and (5) of the Arbitration Act, if the challenge fails the tribunal continues and awards; the party may then seek setting aside of the award on that ground.

q: In a signalling work providing block proving by axle counters at a station, the block section is treated as proved clear for admitting a train only when:

options.A: The number of axles counted as entering the section tallies with the number counted as leaving it, showing that no vehicle is left standing in the section
options.B: The driver of the last train reports verbally that he has cleared the section
options.C: The token for the section has been delivered to the guard of the train
options.D: The home signal of the station has been taken 'off' for the train

e: With block proving by axle counters, the section is proved clear only when axles counted in tally with axles counted out, showing no vehicle is left in the section.

q: A siding taking off from a running line is provided with a trap point at its exit. The trap point serves the purpose that:

options.A: Wagons can be weighed while standing on the siding
options.B: A vehicle moving out of the siding without authority is derailed at the trap before it can foul the running line
options.C: The siding can be used for loading from both ends
options.D: Trains can be received on the siding at a higher speed

e: A trap point at a siding exit derails an unauthorised vehicle moving out of the siding before it can foul the running line, protecting main line movements.

q: On a section where ballast is steadily sinking into a soft formation and mud is pumping up through the ballast under traffic, the engineering remedy provided in the work is a blanket layer over the formation, which works principally by:

options.A: Increasing the speed permissible on the section
options.B: Providing a cushion for the sleepers against impact
options.C: Preventing the intermixing of ballast and formation soil and improving the bearing and drainage of the formation
options.D: Reducing the quantity of ballast required in the section

e: A blanket layer over a soft formation prevents intermixing of ballast and formation soil and improves bearing and drainage, stopping mud pumping under traffic.

q: A contractor stops the curing of a freshly concreted slab after two days on the plea that the concrete has already set. The Engineer directs him to continue curing for the prescribed period because curing is necessary for the concrete:

options.A: To change its colour uniformly
options.B: To dry out as quickly as possible
options.C: To reduce the load coming on the foundation
options.D: To gain its designed strength and durability and to avoid shrinkage cracks

e: Curing keeps concrete moist so it gains its designed strength and durability and avoids shrinkage cracks; mere setting after two days is not sufficient.

q: A retaining wall built to support the bank behind it shows bulging after heavy rain, and weep holes are ordered to be provided through the wall. The weep holes serve to:

options.A: Admit rainwater into the bank for compaction
options.B: Drain out the water accumulating behind the wall and thereby relieve the water pressure on the wall
options.C: Ventilate the foundation of the wall
options.D: Provide a passage for cables behind the wall

e: Weep holes drain water accumulating behind a retaining wall and relieve hydrostatic pressure on the wall, which otherwise causes bulging or failure.

q: A major track renewal on a busy running line can be taken up by the contractor only during a traffic block granted for the work. Such a block means that:

options.A: The contractor may work on the line at any time of the day
options.B: Only goods trains are run on the line during the work
options.C: Train movement on the line is suspended or regulated for the authorised period so that the work can be carried out safely in the possession of the line
options.D: The line is permanently closed to traffic from that date

e: A traffic block is an authorised period when train movement is suspended or regulated so work can be done safely in possession of the line.

q: The drawings for an extension of a station building show a structure coming within the clearance limits prescribed in the Schedule of Dimensions. The correct course before the work is executed is that:

options.A: The work may be executed and the infringement condoned afterwards as a matter of course
options.B: The sectional staff may permit the infringement locally
options.C: The contractor may decide whether the clearance is adequate
options.D: The work must not be executed as proposed; the infringement must either be removed from the design or condonation of the competent authority obtained beforehand

e: A design infringing the Schedule of Dimensions must not be executed; the infringement must be removed or prior condonation of the competent authority obtained.

q: Stone pitching laid on the slope of a high embankment is provided with a toe wall at the foot of the slope. The toe wall serves principally to:

options.A: Hold the pitching in position at its foot and protect the toe of the slope from erosion and slipping
options.B: Mark the boundary of the railway land at that place
options.C: Drain the water collected on top of the embankment
options.D: Support the rails at the top of the embankment

e: A toe wall at the foot of stone pitching holds the pitching in position and protects the toe of the embankment slope from erosion and slipping.

q: On completion of a work, the contractor leaves behind his temporary sheds, surplus materials and debris at the site and does not clear them despite notice. The correct course under the conditions of contract is that:

options.A: The site is accepted as it is, the sheds becoming railway property without any payment or recovery
options.B: The final bill is withheld permanently and the contract is treated as unterminated
options.C: The contractor remains liable to clear and restore the site at his own cost, and on his failure the Railway may get the clearance done and recover the cost from the amounts due to him
options.D: The debris is cleared departmentally at railway cost as a maintenance work

e: Under the GCC, the contractor must clear and restore the site at his own cost; on failure Railways may get it done and recover the cost from amounts due to him.

q: In arbitral proceedings arising out of a works contract, the parties have nowhere agreed to dispense with oral hearings. As regards oral hearing, the position under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is that:

options.A: An arbitral tribunal can never hold an oral hearing
options.B: Oral hearings can be held only with the permission of the court
options.C: The contractor alone can decide whether a hearing will be held
options.D: The arbitral tribunal may hold oral hearings at an appropriate stage of the proceedings, on the request of a party, unless the parties have agreed that no oral hearing shall be held

e: Under Sec 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the tribunal shall hold oral hearings on a party request, unless parties agreed that no oral hearing shall be held.

q: In arbitral proceedings arising out of a works contract, one party complains that it was not given a proper opportunity to present its case before the tribunal. The requirement of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 in this regard is that:

options.A: The parties shall be treated with equality and each party shall be given a full opportunity to present its case
options.B: Only the claimant is required to be given an opportunity of hearing
options.C: The tribunal may decide the case without hearing any party
options.D: Opportunity of hearing is required only if the court so directs

e: Under Sec 18 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, parties shall be treated with equality and each party shall be given a full opportunity to present its case.

q: A dispute under a works contract is taken up in conciliation under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. In conducting the conciliation proceedings, the conciliator:

options.A: Is bound strictly by the Code of Civil Procedure and the Indian Evidence Act
options.B: Is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 or the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, and is guided by principles of objectivity, fairness and justice
options.C: Must decide the dispute finally like an arbitrator
options.D: Can impose a settlement on an unwilling party

e: Under Sec 66 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the conciliator is not bound by the CPC or Evidence Act and is guided by objectivity, fairness and justice.

q: On the expiry of a public-private partnership concession for a project facility, the 'handback' provisions of the concession agreement require the concessionaire to:

options.A: Demolish the facility and remove it from the site
options.B: Sell the facility to the highest bidder in the open market
options.C: Retain the facility against payment of its book value to the authority
options.D: Transfer the project assets and facility back to the authority, in the prescribed working condition and free of encumbrances

e: Handback provisions require the concessionaire to transfer the project assets and facility back to the authority in prescribed working condition, free of encumbrances.

q: A concession agreement for a project is terminated before the end of the concession period and a termination payment becomes due to the concessionaire. The amount of such payment ordinarily depends on:

options.A: Whether the termination has occurred on account of the default of the concessionaire or the default of the authority
options.B: The profit earned by the concessionaire in the previous year
options.C: The number of staff employed on the project
options.D: The value of the stores lying at the site

e: A termination payment under a concession depends on whose default caused termination, concessionaire default or authority default, as the agreement treats the two differently.

q: In a public-private partnership project, the obligation to make available the site and right of way for the project, free of encumbrances, rests ordinarily on:

options.A: The lenders financing the project
options.B: The authority granting the concession, which hands over the site to the concessionaire for execution of the project
options.C: The Independent Engineer appointed for the project
options.D: The contractor engaged for the earthwork of the project

e: In a PPP, the granting authority must make available the project site and right of way free of encumbrances and hand it over to the concessionaire for execution.

q: A buyer objects that goods ordered by him on the Government e-Marketplace were supplied not by GeM itself but by a seller registered on the portal. The position is that:

options.A: GeM itself manufactures and supplies all goods sold on the portal
options.B: GeM supplies goods only for orders above a prescribed value
options.C: GeM is a marketplace portal on which sellers offer their goods and services; the supply against an order is made by the seller on whom the order is placed
options.D: The order should have been placed on the portal's own stores depot

e: GeM is only a marketplace portal; registered sellers offer goods and services on it, and supply against an order is made by the seller on whom the order is placed.

q: Corrigenda and the bids for a works tender handled on IREPS are dealt with in the system so that:

options.A: A corrigendum is communicated only to the tenderer who is likely to be the lowest
options.B: Bids may be submitted on paper in the tender box as an alternative
options.C: A corrigendum takes effect only after the tenders are opened
options.D: A corrigendum to the tender notice is published on the same portal before the closing of the tender, and bids are submitted electronically in the system itself

e: On IREPS, a corrigendum is published on the same portal before tender closing, and bids are submitted electronically in the system itself, not on paper.

q: After the award of a work, a contractor claims extra payment on the ground that he had not anticipated the heavy lead for water and the poor condition of the approach to the site. His claim is not tenable principally because:

options.A: A tenderer is deemed to have visited and inspected the site and satisfied himself about the site conditions and local factors affecting execution before quoting his rates
options.B: Site conditions are guaranteed by the Railways in every tender
options.C: The tender committee should have pointed out the conditions to him
options.D: Extra payment for site conditions is made only from contingencies

e: A tenderer is deemed to have inspected the site and satisfied himself about site conditions and local factors before quoting, so unforeseen lead or approach claims are not tenable.

q: The deliberations of a Tender Committee for a work result in a recommendation for acceptance of a tender. This recommendation is formally brought on record through:

options.A: A verbal intimation given to the successful tenderer
options.B: Minutes of the committee's proceedings, recorded and signed by the members, which are placed before the accepting authority
options.C: A note in the personal diary of the convenor of the committee
options.D: An entry in the Measurement Book of the work

e: Tender Committee recommendations are formally recorded in minutes of its proceedings, signed by the members and placed before the accepting authority.

q: Before the foundations of a major bridge are designed, bore holes are drilled at the site and the strata met with are logged. This soil investigation is carried out in order to ascertain:

options.A: The quantity of cement required for the work
options.B: The rates payable for the earthwork of the approaches
options.C: The colour of the soil at the site
options.D: The nature of the strata and the safe bearing capacity available for founding the structure

e: Soil investigation by bore holes logs the strata to ascertain their nature and the safe bearing capacity available for founding a major bridge.

q: Excavation for a deep foundation is in progress and the sides of the pit show signs of caving in. The step immediately required at the site is that:

options.A: The sides of the excavation are properly supported by shoring and strutting so that the excavation does not collapse and endanger the workmen
options.B: The excavation is deepened quickly before the sides cave in
options.C: The workmen are asked to work only in the centre of the pit
options.D: The measurements of the excavation are recorded at once

e: Excavation sides showing signs of caving must be supported at once by shoring and strutting to prevent collapse and danger to workmen, a basic site safety duty.

q: Reinforcement bars in the roof slab of a building are found placed almost flush with the bottom face of the slab, and the contractor is directed to relay them with the prescribed cover of concrete. The cover to reinforcement is provided in order to:

options.A: Reduce the quantity of steel required in the slab
options.B: Protect the steel from corrosion and fire and to ensure proper bond with the concrete
options.C: Make the slab thinner than designed
options.D: Facilitate the removal of shuttering

e: Concrete cover protects reinforcement from corrosion and fire and ensures proper bond with concrete, so bars cannot be left flush with the slab face.

q: At the site of a work, samples of each batch of fresh concrete being placed are taken and a slump test is performed on them. The slump test serves to check:

options.A: The compressive strength of the hardened concrete
options.B: The quantity of cement in the concrete
options.C: The consistency and workability of the fresh concrete
options.D: The rate at which the concrete will set

e: The slump test checks the consistency and workability of fresh concrete; it does not measure strength, cement content or setting rate.

q: Concrete being laid in a deep beam of a structure is compacted by the site staff with a needle vibrator as the concrete is placed. Compaction of fresh concrete by vibration serves principally to:

options.A: Expel the entrapped air from the concrete and make it dense, free of honeycombing and well filled around the reinforcement
options.B: Increase the water content of the concrete
options.C: Make the concrete set instantaneously on placing
options.D: Separate the coarse aggregate from the mortar in the mix

e: Vibration compacts fresh concrete by expelling entrapped air, making it dense, free of honeycombing and well filled around reinforcement.

q: The foundation pit of a structure is full of accumulated water and concrete is proposed to be laid in it. The correct course is that:

options.A: Concrete is laid in the standing water without any precaution
options.B: The water is pumped out by dewatering and the foundation is laid in dry condition, as required
options.C: Extra cement is added and the concrete is laid in water
options.D: The work is abandoned till the next dry season in all cases

e: Foundation concrete must be laid dry; accumulated water must be pumped out by dewatering first, as laying in standing water weakens the foundation.

q: To verify that the concrete being laid in a structure is attaining the required strength, the site staff get test cubes cast from the concrete and tested. The cube results represent:

options.A: The strength of the steel used in the structure
options.B: The bearing capacity of the soil under the foundation
options.C: The compressive strength of the concrete placed in the work
options.D: The workability of the fresh concrete

e: Test cubes cast from concrete placed in the work represent its compressive strength when tested, which is the check for required strength.

q: The top strata at the site of a bridge are weak and incapable of bearing the load of the piers, and pile foundations are adopted for the bridge. Pile foundations are used in such a case because they:

options.A: Require no soil investigation before design
options.B: Are the cheapest foundation in every situation
options.C: Float the structure on the top soil itself
options.D: Transfer the load of the structure through the weak strata to deeper firm strata

e: Pile foundations transfer the load of the structure through weak top strata to deeper firm strata capable of bearing it.

q: The piers of a bridge across a river are founded on well foundations. A well foundation is a foundation which:

options.A: Is spread out widely just below the river bed
options.B: Is sunk through the soil, in the form of a hollow well or caisson, to a firm stratum below the scour level, and is then plugged and capped to carry the pier
options.C: Is built entirely above the water level of the river
options.D: Consists only of timber piles driven in the bed

e: A well foundation is sunk as a hollow well or caisson to a firm stratum below scour level, then plugged and capped to carry the bridge pier.

q: Foundation work for a structure has to be executed in a river where water is flowing. A cofferdam is put up around the site of the foundation. A cofferdam is:

options.A: A permanent dam built across the river for irrigation
options.B: A type of pile used in the foundation
options.C: A temporary enclosure made in the water and pumped dry, so that the foundation work can be executed in dry condition inside it
options.D: A machine used for drilling bore holes in the bed

e: A cofferdam is a temporary enclosure built in water and pumped dry so foundation work can be executed in dry condition inside it.

q: In a newly built quarter, dampness is seen rising from the ground into the walls above the plinth, and a damp-proof course is ordered at plinth level. A damp-proof course serves to:

options.A: Strengthen the foundation of the building
options.B: Carry the load of the walls to the ground
options.C: Improve the appearance of the plinth
options.D: Prevent the moisture from the ground rising into the walls above by capillary action

e: A damp-proof course at plinth level prevents ground moisture rising into walls above by capillary action, stopping dampness in the building.

q: A work for providing an in-motion weighbridge at a goods terminal is sanctioned. An in-motion weighbridge serves the purpose of:

options.A: Weighing the passengers' luggage at the station
options.B: Checking the speed of trains passing over it
options.C: Counting the wagons in a passing train
options.D: Weighing loaded wagons while they are in motion, for charge of freight and detection of overloading

e: An in-motion weighbridge weighs loaded wagons while in motion, for freight charging and detection of overloading at goods terminals.

q: In a yard remodelling work, a turntable is provided in the locomotive area of the yard. A turntable is used for:

options.A: Turning a locomotive or vehicle end to end so that it faces the opposite direction
options.B: Lifting a locomotive for repairs in the shed
options.C: Weighing locomotives before they go on line
options.D: Washing the undergear of locomotives

e: A turntable turns a locomotive or vehicle end to end so that it faces the opposite direction, in the locomotive area of a yard.

q: At a station where coaching rakes are stabled at the platform line, a washable apron is provided under the platform line in a works estimate. A washable apron is provided so that:

options.A: Passengers can walk safely beside the train
options.B: The coaches standing at the platform can be washed and cleaned and the washings drained away, keeping the platform line clean
options.C: The platform surface can be raised to the level of the coach floor
options.D: Goods can be loaded into the coaches from the platform

e: A washable apron under a platform line allows coaches stabled there to be washed and cleaned and the washings drained away, keeping the line clean.

q: In the layout of a coaching yard, one of the lines is designated as the sick line. The sick line is the line on which:

options.A: Empty rakes are stabled overnight
options.B: Rakes are washed before despatch
options.C: Coaches and wagons requiring repairs or attention are placed and attended to
options.D: Locomotives are kept ready for trains

e: The sick line is where coaches and wagons requiring repairs or attention are placed and attended to in a coaching yard.

q: For carrying out work on the overhead equipment of an electrified section, a power block is taken. A power block, as distinct from a traffic block, means that:

options.A: Only the signals of the section are replaced to 'on'
options.B: Road traffic at the level crossings is stopped
options.C: The train services are diverted to another route
options.D: The traction power supply to the overhead equipment of the section is switched off and the equipment earthed, so that work can be done on it safely

e: A power block means traction power to the overhead equipment is switched off and the equipment earthed, so OHE work can be done safely.

q: At an interlocked lifting-barrier level crossing provided in a signalling work, the lifting barriers are interlocked with the signals so that:

options.A: The signal for a train cannot be taken 'off' unless the barriers are closed against road traffic, and the barriers cannot be opened while the signal is 'off'
options.B: The barriers can be lifted at any time by the gateman
options.C: Road vehicles can pass while the signal is 'off' for a train
options.D: The signals work automatically without the gateman

e: Interlocking ensures the signal cannot be taken off unless lifting barriers are closed to road traffic, and barriers cannot open while the signal is off.

q: In the drawings of a road over-bridge to be built in place of a level crossing, the headroom available under the bridge is shown. 'Headroom' in this context means:

options.A: The height of the parapet of the bridge above the deck
options.B: The length of the bridge between the abutments
options.C: The vertical clearance between the road surface below and the underside of the bridge structure, available for the passage of road vehicles
options.D: The depth of the foundation of the bridge below the road

e: Headroom under a road over-bridge is the vertical clearance between the road surface below and the underside of the bridge structure for road vehicles.

q: In the estimate of a bridge, provision is made for its ventway. The ventway of a bridge refers to:

options.A: The passage provided for pedestrians on the bridge
options.B: The opening left in the parapet for drainage of the deck
options.C: The space occupied by the girders of the bridge
options.D: The total opening available under the bridge for the passage of water

e: Ventway of a bridge is the total opening available under the bridge for the passage of water.

q: At a bridge across a river, guide bunds are provided on the approaches in the works estimate. Guide bunds serve to:

options.A: Guide the river flow smoothly and in the intended direction through the waterway of the bridge and protect the approaches from erosion
options.B: Guide road vehicles on to the bridge
options.C: Support the girders of the bridge
options.D: Store the water of the river for use in the colony

e: Guide bunds guide river flow smoothly in the intended direction through the bridge waterway and protect the approaches from erosion.

q: An end-loading ramp is provided at the end of a siding at a station in a works programme. Such a ramp is used for:

options.A: Loading passengers' luggage into brake vans
options.B: Driving wheeled vehicles, such as road vehicles and machinery, on to flat wagons for despatch by rail
options.C: Unloading coal from wagons by gravity
options.D: Stacking parcels before loading

e: An end-loading ramp at a siding end lets wheeled vehicles such as road vehicles and machinery be driven on to flat wagons for despatch by rail.
